goals: Deliver receipt-bound Linux guest exit checks using a source-pinned Testudo image and the fixed pad-guest-check-v1 SSH subsystem.
Preserve native attended consent or scoped standing preauthorization, mandatory containment, and no host fallback for an explicit Linux request.
Re-evaluate the removed launcher and transport against merged core rather than replaying their historical implementation blindly.
currentGenerationRule: The authenticated workflow claim binds task, step, epoch, writer, dispatch, receipt commit and output/check digests. Native request and backend job IDs are exclusive durable intents. Before launching, re-authenticate the current claim and authorization; the pinned supervisor checks the same bundle/check identity. A prior job ID or unknown effect is not reusable and cannot authorize a replacement generation. Cancellation fences acceptance even if a child finishes late.
initialConditions: Actors: workflow authority and reducer, native admission adapter, SSH BatchMode transport, unprivileged Linux launcher, Firecracker process, pinned Testudo PID1 and containment monitor, unprivileged check child, and owner installer.
Each execution session has one authenticated claim, one native request ID and one exclusive backend job directory; resource reassignment requires a new identity, not a cleared prior intent.
The backend is the owner-selected Linux target from private runtime configuration only. No real guest runs on the development host.

Required prior to live execution: independently reviewed source-pinned image recipe, artifact manifest with actual kernel/image/initramfs/taxonomy/Firecracker digests, fixed check-ID map, and owner-installed subsystem/runtime.

Image and initramfs pins are checked before the boot effect. The protected guest channel must report the exact bundle/check identity and armed taxonomy before a result is eligible. Verified teardown precedes pass.

Testudo main was observed at 92796bc7d487b6c0a8b9128be87653f17898742b during initial discovery. Its current guest protocol is not evidence of an existing PAD check-image builder or compatible release.
exclusions: No changes to package.json or lockfiles, no secrets or personal target values in tracked files, no owner payload replacement, no raw remote-shell execution lane.
No edits to a separate Testudo checkout are inferred from this PAD assignment; the image recipe must identify its source dependencies and any required separately reviewed upstream work.
No live acceptance claim from local fake-VMM, serial-fixture, unit-test, diagram or abstract-model results.
failureCases: Wrong or missing image/initramfs/taxonomy pins, absent or late armed marker, containment trip with exit126, forged result origin, command substitution, bundle substitution, log digest mismatch.

Disconnect or watchdog after launch, cancellation before launch or during execution, revoked standing preauthorization between runs or before acceptance, incomplete teardown, duplicate job, unknown prior effect, and a late result for an obsolete claim.
progressRequirements: Test first; preserve the merged core's authenticated loader, standing authorization and terminal-state fences.
Run named positive and negative model controls, actual CLI/Pi/reducer conformance, full Node/Python suites and audited native/shared gates without environment skips presented as passes.
When the reviewed installable runtime is ready, record exact backend installation commands in the private checkpoint and POST for the owner relay; do not perform the owner installation.
Keep raw evidence and uncertainty visible; deliver a draft PR only.
scope: PAD guest adapter/transport and fixed backend launcher with test and model correspondence.
Reproducible source-pinned Testudo image recipe, protected guest serial protocol and immutable artifact-manifest contract.
Backend-independent verification can proceed while reviewed image/backend prerequisites are unavailable.
intendedRollback: Before live installation, preserve core's unavailable behavior. After an uncertain launch or containment trip, retain job evidence and refuse reuse; owner-held recovery or a normal reviewed revert is required. Do not delete relied-on artifacts or kill unrelated processes.
